node.comment: Before coming into this class, I would say that I was a fairly confident speaker and was looking forward to improving my skills, however I feel like this class did the opposite. Glenny is an incredibly picky and biased professor and grader. She makes it obvious that she favors the men in that class and made passive agressive comments to the women.

Please avoid at all costs. There are other public speaking professors to choose from. 

Dr. Glenny is unkind, strict, and not gracious. She speaks in a demeaning manner to her students and is often rude. She takes off a lot of points for small mistakes. I heard her make sexist and anti-Semitic remarks. 

I and my friends were truly scared of her.

If you are not on Glenny's good side, good luck. She has a clear bais towards students who she does not like, typically females, and tends to grade them more harshley. I can say withouth a doubt, she favored engineering students. She gave feedback publically. Overall, you should avoid Glenny if you can, she is very biased hard to understand.

She grades very harshly on speeches in Public Speaking, so make sure you follow all of her guidelines. It's not about if you have a good speech, it's if she thinks you followed instructions well enough. Get on her good side.

I asked Prof. Glenny for an excused absence for my grandfather's FUNERAL, and she refused because it wasn't a school-related event. I know it wasn't an actual policy for the university because all my other professors gave me excused absences. 
She also had clear biases and was the most condescending professor I have ever met.

One of the things that scare students about Professor Glenny is that she is very honest; she will tell you what to do to make your work better. I know she isn't for everyone, but I loved her honors public speaking class! Easily my favorite class of the year! If you want a professor who will challenge your limits, Glenny is perfect for just that.

I have never had a professor looking for such specific criteria, yet explaining it so poorly. I had a verbally abusive meeting with her over the final, where she made up expectations, and told me that "I didn't deserve to be in the honors program." For some this class will be fine— but don't play Russian roulette with if she will like you or not!
node.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

node.comment: She initially mentioned during the first week she was a tough grader but I never received a grade lower than an A on any speech (and I am not a strong public speaker). She is EXTREMELY meticulous and detail oriented, but everything is laid out in samples that she gives to you before hand. If you follow the sample you should have no issue.

Glenny was not a good teacher. As a person in disability services, I did get graded less harsh than other students, but she would roughly criticize my peers. I did not feel comfortable presenting in her class because of this. She also made racist and sexist comments and would favor the men in sports in the class.

Professor has a clear bias, I feel this is appropriate to say considering this was one of the things she described about herself when introducing it to the class. She gave inconsistent feedback and I am fairly sure some of her comments were borderline racist. Do not take this professor she is unfit for her profession.

So to introduce the class she said this is an easy class and that she gives out a lot of A's and B's. Well I don't know a single person in the class that would describe this class as easy.  She clearly had favorites in the class and I understand rewarding good students but she didn't give those she didn't like a chance.

Dr. Glenny is one of my favorite professors! Public Speaking was a really fun course to take, and the textbook is super easy to read, formatted similar to a novel. Although I was nervous to take this course, it turned out to be one of my favorites this semester. As long as you turn your work in on time and staple your papers, you'll do great.

I would not recommend this professor to my worst enemy. She is borderline abusive to her students. She was cold when I made a mistake on a paper outline (that cost my grade). I know for a fact she made at least several students (including myself) cry after class. She claims she is available for questions, but mocks you for asking an "obvious one."

I was super nervous for her public speaking class, but as long as you are interested in learning and follow her guidelines, you're golden! She loves what she does and has good feedback if she knows you want the feedback to get better.

Many people say that she's an unfair grader, but if you carefully read the assignment sheets, you will be fine. You receive the grade appropriate for how well you followed instructions and the amount of effort you put into it. While it's a bit of a difficult class from the grading, it makes you a better public speaker and a much better student.

Worst Professor I have ever had. You lose points for things like no staple in papers or something not being aligned on an outline. She gives no helpful feedback and I felt like I did not improve one bit as a public speaker. I got docked points because she thought I did not mention something, when in reality I did.
node.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

node.comment: I would not recommend Dr. Glenny. I noticed that peoples grades would depend on the mood she was in. Some people did not give very well organized speeches and got a good grade if they spoke when she was in a good mood. She would give one critique one day and say the opposite the next. She seems like a good person, but she is not a good professor!

Dr. Glenny isn't very professional. She may come off that way but after every speech, she calls everyone individually to attention to tell them what they did right and wrong, and typically only speaks to what they did wrong. The way she does it is rude and humiliating. She also either likes students or hates them and it isn't based on anything.

Glenny treats her class like a job and is a horrible boss. If it were a real life situation I wouldn't work for her. She doesn't help you when you ask questions and will wonder why you did the assignment wrong. She is the type of person to smile in your face then shred you to pieces in critiques and or emails. Don't recommend her as a professor.

I'll admit, I did not like Prof. Glenny the first couple weeks; however, I did end up liking her a lot. She helped me improve my public speaking skills. Just follow her instructions, and you will do fine. She was pretty accessible by emails, but I think she prefers it if you talk to her in class. Overall, she has high expectations, but she is great
node.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader
